newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour plans 10 bln stg from utility tax - paper.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour plans 10 bln stg from utility tax - paper.

text.p: The UK opposition Labour Party plans to raise 10 billion stg through its utility tax -- double the original estimate -- according to a report in the Independent on Sunday newspaper.

The unsourced report said that shadow Chancellor of the Exchequer, Gordon Brown, will announce on Monday plans to go-ahead with a one-off tax hit on UK privatised companies in his first Budget, if Labour is elected.
Labour is currently well ahead of the ruling Conservative Party in opinion polls, with an election due by May this year.
The report said the tax net will be widened to raise more than the three to five billion stg originally envisaged.
Companies including British Telecommunications Plc, airports group BAA Plc and Associated British Ports Holdings Plc are all expected to be hit as well as utility companies, said the report.
But a spokesman for the Labour Party told Reuters on Sunday that any reports on the tax's impact at this stage were "purely speculative and should not be taken seriously."
The spokesman confirmed that Brown is due to give a speech on Monday on public spending, but declined to comment further.

The Independent on Sunday report said that Labour is confident of being able to push through the so-called "windfall-tax" on the bumper profits from privatised utilities and has enlisted the help of top business and legal experts to ensure that it cannot be challenged in court.
A separate report in the Mail on Sunday said that bosses of U.S.-owned utilities in the UK were preparing a political offensive to block Labour's windfall tax.

The report said some U.S. chiefs had already met at the U.S. embassy in London to discuss threats of trade sanctions against UK companies investing in American companies as a possible retaliatory measure.
But there was no named source for the report. --London newsroom +44 171 5427717
